findings.title: Capture agent declares no DPI awareness; click, screenshot and UIA-rect coordinate frames depend on whichever third-party library initializes first
findings.evidence: Grep `DPI|dpi|SetProcess|SetThread|shcore|GetDpiForWindow` over all *.py in the repo -> no matches; sopforge.spec:29 `runtime_hooks=[]`. recorder.py:141-153 `element, window = resolve_at(x, y)` / `self._shots.capture(x, y)` / `screen_x, screen_y = x - origin_x, y - origin_y` and the same subtraction on `bounding_rect` -- pixel offsets only, no scale factor; pywinauto is imported lazily at uia.py:71 on the first click, after the pynput hook is installed. Whether pywinauto changes the process DPI context on import could not be checked (shell denied), so the 'frame depends on import order' part remains an unverified risk, as peer A-09 notes. tests/test_recorder.py:152-156 cover 100%-scale, non-negative origins only.
findings.proposed_fix: At the top of `capture/__main__.py` call `ctypes.windll.user32.SetProcessDpiAwarenessContext(-4)` (PER_MONITOR_AWARE_V2) with `shcore.SetProcessDpiAwareness(2)` fallback so hooks, mss and pywinauto share one physical-pixel frame; record `screen.scale` in the manifest; add negative-origin and mixed-DPI cases to test_recorder.py.

findings.title: A click outside every monitor rect is silently attributed to monitor 1 and translated by monitor 1's origin; only reachable if hook and mss coordinate frames disagree
findings.evidence: shots.py:25-36 `monitor_for_point`: docstring 'falls back to 1 if the point isn't inside any known monitor rect'; loop over `sct.monitors[1:]` then `return 1`; :56-57 `monitor = sct.monitors[monitor_idx]; origin = (monitor["left"], monitor["top"])`; recorder.py:143 subtracts that origin. Peer A-09/F-12 dispute is partly right: Windows confines the cursor to the monitor union, so with pynput and mss in the same DPI context this branch is unreachable; it fires only under the F-11 frame-mismatch precondition, which I could not demonstrate. Retained as low because the fallback is silent (no log, no manifest flag) when it does fire -- the peer's own point that clamping could conceal the coordinate defect argues for making it visible, not for leaving it silent.
findings.proposed_fix: Log a warning and set a manifest flag when `monitor_for_point` falls through to 1 so a frame mismatch becomes visible rather than silently mis-placing the marker; fix the frame itself per F-11 rather than clamping to a different monitor.

findings.evidence: server.py:412-413 sets `narrative_text = None` when `generate_narrative` raises (e.g. Ollama unreachable -- ollama_probe.txt:5), while :444 still passes `claims=claims` (non-empty: synthetic narration always yields claims). :646-652 selects `polish_section` when `[polish].enabled` or a `?polish=local|haiku` rerender override; :654 `md_narrative_text = narrative_text`; :659 `generate_polish_fields(None, step_results, polish_llm)` -> polish.py:421-422 `(narrative_text, [])` for falsy input, returns None either via :446-448 (LLM failure) or :465-467 `_splice_verify_lines(None, [])` -> :361-362 `return body_text`. server.py:680 `ok, missing = validate_claim_coverage(md_narrative_text, claims)` -> claim_coverage.py:84 `_claim_covered(claim, final_text)` -> :23 `stripped.lower() in text.lower()` with `text=None` -> AttributeError. jobs.py:69-72 catches it and marks the job `error`; `doc.md` (:692) is never written. Contradicts the :412 comment 'narrative is best-effort, never blocks the doc'. Static trace (shell denied both rounds); peer A-05's independent probe reproduced `AttributeError 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'lower'`.
findings.proposed_fix: Guard at server.py:680: `ok, missing = validate_claim_coverage(md_narrative_text or "", claims)` (or skip the check when `narrative_text is None`), and combine with F-02's fix so a failed narrative still emits [verify] blockquotes; add a test with polish enabled and a raising narrative stub asserting the job finishes and doc.md exists.
